translations.answer: The provided solutions are to enter root, re-source ROS and workspace environment, and restart. This approach grants broader permissions. A more cautious approach is to first confirm real-time scheduling permissions (Real-Time Scheduling Permission), ulimit, user group permissions, and minimal capabilities required for the system, and only authorize components that are necessary. This post cannot be considered a formal solution until official documentation or reproducible experiments are confirmed.
translations.applicability: This is applicable for Linux real-time scheduling permission errors. The specific authorization method depends on deployment and security policies.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent reproducibility is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Complete the missing ros-noetic-navigation, python3-catkin-tools or Python modules, and use -DPYTHON_EXECUTABLE=/usr/bin/python3 to fix the interpreter.
translations.details.attempts.1: The comment suggests using root to bypass the sched_setscheduler permission; this approach is too broad and only considered as a candidate for further validation, not a recommended solution.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Compile and run the DDP/SQP example of OCS2, then separately compile legged_controllers, Gazebo, and real machine hardware packages. Each terminal must explicitly source ROS and workspace environment; retain the first error rather than only the final chain of errors.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Cross-reference the text, 7 visible comments, and one image. The community experience has not been independently verified by official documentation, source code, or issue.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The text provides corresponding commands for missing move_base_msgs, catkin-tools, and empy/Python interpreter. Whether this applies to the current distribution requires further verification.
translations.details.environments.0: Ubuntu + ROS Noetic; catkin-tools; OCS2, Pinocchio, hpp-fcl; Unitree A1 Gazebo simulation.
translations.details.limits.0: The article is intended for ROS Noetic and older dependency combinations. Directly switching system Python or running the entire control stack as root may pollute the environment or expand permissions.
translations.details.limits.1: The comment cannot be linked separately; only the root post link and visible comments should be retained.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The text forms a layered startup path from the OCS2 example, controller, simulation, to real machine dependencies. The real-time scheduling permission and 'falling on the ground' issue have not been sufficiently closed-looped.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: The first compilation of legged_control / OCS2 encounters missing packages, Python modules, or catkin commands. How to locate issues by layer?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: The controller starts with permission denied for sched_setscheduler. Should it be run as root?
translations.details.problem_statements.2: The robot moves on the ground in simulation. Does the post provide sufficient diagnostic information?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Prioritize verifying ulimit, group permissions, and minimal Linux capabilities when dealing with real-time scheduling. Do not consider 'sudo su and run the entire control stack' as a default approach.
translations.details.safety_notes.1: Limit the robot to a lower speed, lower force, and set emergency stop before deployment in simulation and lifting conditions, and record joint and contact logs.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Missing dependencies, incorrect Python interpreter, terminal not sourced, or insufficient real-time scheduling capability or resource limits.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The 'falling on the ground' motion lacks control mode, joint state, contact force, and logs. It is not reliable to diagnose at this stage.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Missing move_base_msgs, rospkg, defusedxml, empy, or catkin; no permission for real-time scheduling interface; robot moves on the ground.
translations.media_summaries.0: The text has a single engineering diagram for showing optional gait/control modes. The image does not provide joint, contact force, or optimizer logs, so it cannot explain the 'falling on the ground' symptom in the comment.
